content.title: The Score: Warner Bros., GameStop, Campbell’s, Lululemon and More Stocks That Defined the Week
content.summary: Paramount Skydance  on Monday made a $77.9 billion hostile takeover bid for all of  Warner Bros. Discovery  escalating its battle against  Netflix  for the storied entertainment giant.  Netflix on Dec. 5 agreed to buy Warner Bros. for $72 billion after Warner splits its studios and HBO Max streaming business from its cable networks.  Paramount, run by  David Ellison,  is arguing that its all-cash offer for all of Warner is a better deal for shareholders and more likely to pass regulatory muster.

content.title: Does Profit Growth On Falling Sales And Collectibles Momentum Change The Bull Case For GameStop (GME)?
content.summary: GameStop Corp. has reported fiscal third-quarter 2025 results, with sales easing to US$821 million from US$860.3 million a year earlier, while net income rose to US$77.1 million and diluted earnings per share increased to US$0.13 from US$0.04. The quarter underlined an earnings-driven turnaround powered by tighter cost controls and growing collectibles sales, even as core hardware and software revenues continued to weaken.
